synthesis.summary: Key intersections center on dermaplaning: high information needs and safety concerns coincide, creating conversion and reputation risk if guidance is unclear; retail deal content drives purchases but coupon/availability friction can block conversion.

findings.title: Dermaplaning conversion is gated by safety fears + routine uncertainty
findings.business_implication: Without clear pre/post-care instructions and risk framing, dermaplaning content can attract high-engagement warnings and adverse-experience reports that deter would-be buyers and undermine product credibility.
findings.recommended_action_area: Add standardized dermaplaning safety guidance (skin prep, sanitation, frequency, contraindications, aftercare) in captions/creator talking points and landing pages; consider dermatologist/educational co-sign content.

findings.title: Promo-driven buying intent exists, but availability/coupon friction can stall it
findings.business_implication: Deal content can convert quickly, but missing coupons and hard-to-find attachments/refills create drop-off and can redirect shoppers to alternatives.
findings.recommended_action_area: Tighten retail execution: ensure coupon distribution clarity, add 'where to buy' + refill/attachment availability guidance, and provide store-locator/refill SKU references in creator posts.

findings.title: Creator-brand fit risk: ad cynicism intersects with purchase intent for pocket razor
findings.business_implication: Even when a product triggers 'need' intent, perceived hypocrisy/value conflict in sponsorship can dampen trust and reduce downstream conversion.
findings.recommended_action_area: Improve partnership framing: align messaging with creator’s stated values (e.g., choice/autonomy), avoid beauty-pressure cues, and emphasize practical/optional use cases.

faq_gaps.summary: Information gaps focus on where to buy, whether refills/attachments exist, coupon eligibility, and proper pre/post-shave routine (especially for dermaplaning to avoid irritation).

synthesis.summary: Key intersections: conversion-ready demand is being shaped by strong information gaps; authenticity improves when creators show real usage; and certain messaging frames (myth-busting / 'women should be hairless') spark backlash that can suppress intent.

findings.title: High intent, but conversion is blocked by where-to-buy / price / refill mechanics questions
findings.business_implication: Shoppers are ready to act but may drop off without immediate availability clarity (retailer, region), transparent pricing/promotions, and simple refill/replace explanations.
findings.recommended_action_area: Retail/distribution messaging + creator toolkits: standardized ‘where to buy’ by country, promo callouts, and a simple carousel/video explaining refills (handle vs blades/soap) and model differences.

findings.title: Authenticity uplift when creators show real hair/use; reduces partnership skepticism and boosts ‘add to cart’ behavior
findings.business_implication: Demonstration realism functions as a credibility lever in a category often criticized for unrealistic shaving visuals; can increase trust and short-cycle purchase intent.
findings.recommended_action_area: Creative guidance: encourage ‘real shave’ demos, second-use check-ins, and close-ups that address nicks/irritation claims with practical technique.

findings.title: Body-hair ‘freedom’ messaging can backfire when paired with product push, triggering organic backlash and credibility challenges
findings.business_implication: Even without coordinated brigading, repeated ideological callouts can dominate comment sections and refract the brand into ‘profiting from insecurities,’ risking reduced effectiveness of empowerment-led campaigns.
findings.recommended_action_area: Messaging calibration: separate empowerment editorial content from hard selling; add explicit choice framing (including opting out), and link to evidence for claims (e.g., myth-busting sources, study methodology).

faq_gaps.summary: Information gaps cluster around where to buy, pricing, blade/soap replacement mechanics, suitability for body zones (incl. bikini), and links to cited research data.
